title: Git Branching Fundamentals
learning_objectives: Explain what Git branches are and why they enable parallel development
Create new branches using `git branch` and `git checkout -b`
Switch between branches and understand HEAD pointer behavior
List branches with `git branch` and identify the active branch
Understand branch naming conventions (feature/, bugfix/, hotfix/)
Apply feature branch workflow to CatchBook development
outline: Introduction: Why branches matter for CatchBook development
What are branches? Understanding pointers and commit history divergence
Switching branches: `git checkout` and `git switch` (modern alternative)
The HEAD pointer: tracking your current location
Hands-on: Create feature branch for CatchBook documentation update

catchbook_context.deliverable: Create feature/update-readme branch with enhanced CatchBook documentation

criteria: Make commits on feature branch without affecting main
Switch between branches and verify different working tree states
Use git log --graph to visualize branch structure
Explain why branches are essential for multi-developer CatchBook work

professor_constraints: Use CatchBook repository for all examples
Emphasize that branches enable fearless experimentation
Show git log --graph visualization at least 3 times during lesson
Demonstrate branch switching changes working directory files
Connect branching to real CatchBook development scenarios (species model, photo upload, etc.)
Avoid overwhelming with rebase/cherry-pick (defer to P01-M02-L04)
